desc:
Given a binary array bits (each element is 0 or 1), count the contiguous subarrays in which the number of 1s is strictly greater than the number of 0s.

bits = [1, 0, 1]
qualifying subarrays: [1] (first), [1] (last), [1, 0, 1]
result = 3
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit integer
hints: Map each 1 to +1 and each 0 to -1. A subarray has more ones than zeros exactly when its mapped sum is positive.
With prefix sums P, you need the number of pairs i < j with P[j] > P[i]. Counting them with a hash map and a sort or tree gives O(n log n) - but the prefix sum only changes by ±1 each step.
Maintain less, the number of earlier prefixes smaller than the current prefix value. When the prefix goes up by one from s, add count[s] to less; when it goes down to s-1, subtract count[s-1].
editorial: After mapping 1 to +1 and 0 to -1 the problem asks for the number of pairs of prefix sums P[i] < P[j] with i < j. A naive count is O(n2), and a general counting structure (BIT or sorted list) gives O(n log n).

Because consecutive prefix sums differ by exactly 1, we can maintain the number less of earlier prefix values that are strictly below the current value in O(1) per step. Going from value s to s+1, the earlier prefixes equal to s become 'less', so add cnt[s]; going from s to s-1, the earlier prefixes equal to s-1 are no longer below, so subtract cnt[s-1]. After each step add less to the answer and increment cnt for the new value. The total is O(n) time and O(n) space.
